## Verifiable evidence bundles

Evidence bundles attach externally verifiable evidence to an existing claim by digest alone. The raw evidence bytes are never accepted, persisted, or logged — only the digest algorithm/value, media type, and a metadata object are stored. Bundles are immutable and append-only: there is no update or delete path.

- `POST /v1/evidence-bundles` — create a bundle with an existing `claim_id`, a non-empty `evidence_type`, `digest_algorithm`, `digest_hex`, a non-empty `media_type`, and a JSON-object `metadata`. Only `digest_algorithm=sha256` with exactly 64 hexadecimal characters is accepted (hex is case-normalized, as for contents). The first creation returns `201` with the stable bundle id, claim association, evidence type, digest algorithm and value, media type, metadata, and UTC `created_at`; a repeat submission with the same claim, evidence type, and digest returns `200` with the existing bundle — its first-submission metadata and media type are retained — and adds no audit event. Any different field combination forms an independent bundle.
- `GET /v1/evidence-bundles/{evidence_bundle_id}` — full public fields, or `404 evidence_bundle_not_found`.
- `GET /v1/evidence-bundles?claim_id=...&evidence_type=...&media_type=...&digest_hex=...&limit=...&cursor=...` — read-only reviewer search over all existing evidence bundles. The success body is `{"items", "count", "next_cursor"}`, each item being the existing evidence-bundle public view (associations, digest algorithm/value, media type, metadata, and UTC `created_at`; evidence bytes are never stored and so are never echoed), in the bundles' stable creation order. Optional `claim_id`, `evidence_type`, and `media_type` are non-empty, case/whitespace-sensitive exact matches that combine as logical AND (absent means unfiltered); `digest_hex` must be exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters (uppercase, padded, or wrong-length spellings are `422`, never normalized). `count` is the filtered total independent of the page. `limit` is a pure decimal integer from 1 to 100 defaulting to 50; `cursor` is an opaque HMAC-signed server token that binds to every effective filter and the limit, so pages resume without duplication or omission and the final page carries `next_cursor: null`. Blank/illegal/repeated/undeclared parameters and an empty, whitespace-only, malformed, tampered, foreign-family, or query-mismatching `cursor` are `422 validation_error` (nothing is silently defaulted); no match is an empty collection with `count` 0, not a 404, and filter values are never resolved for existence. The query and its failures write no bundle, resource, or audit row.
- `GET /v1/claims/{claim_id}/evidence-bundles` — that claim's bundles only, in stable creation order as `{"items", "count"}`; an unknown claim id is `404 claim_not_found` (a missing claim is never an empty collection).
- `GET /v1/contents/{content_id}/evidence-bundles?evidence_type=...&media_type=...&limit=...&cursor=...` — read-only listing for reviewers of the evidence attached to one content. It returns only bundles linked through claims that directly assert this exact content; it does not traverse lineage to ancestor/descendant contents and never returns raw bytes. Optional `evidence_type` and `media_type` are non-empty, case/whitespace-sensitive exact matches that combine as logical AND; absent means unfiltered. Results follow the bundles' stable creation order (across all of the content's claims) as `{"items", "count", "next_cursor"}` where each item is the existing evidence-bundle public view and `count` is the filtered total, independent of the page. `limit` is an integer from 1 to 100 defaulting to 50; `cursor` is an opaque HMAC-signed server token that binds to the origin and every effective filter/limit, so pages resume without duplication or omission and the final page carries `next_cursor: null`. Blank/illegal/repeated/mismatching parameters and an empty, malformed, tampered, foreign-family, or query-mismatching `cursor` are `422 validation_error` (nothing is silently defaulted); an unknown content id is `404 content_not_found`. The query writes no resource or audit rows.
- `GET /v1/contents/{content_id}/export` — read-only provenance-evidence snapshot of one content, for handover to third-party verifiers. The success body is exactly `{"content", "claims"}`: `content` is the full public content view, and `claims` lists the claims that directly assert this exact content in stable creation order, each as the full public claim view plus an `evidence_bundles` array of that claim's bundles in stable creation order (each the full public bundle view). No lineage traversal is performed and no other content, claim, or bundle is ever included; raw content, claim payloads, and evidence bytes never appear. A content without claims yields `"claims": []`; a claim without bundles yields an empty `evidence_bundles` array. The route accepts no query parameters — any parameter is `422 validation_error` — and an unknown content id is `404 content_not_found`. Reads, empty results, and failures write no resource or audit rows.
- `GET /v1/contents/{content_id}/evidence-coverage` — read-only evidence-coverage summary of one content. The request carries no body and no query parameters: any body bytes (even whitespace or malformed JSON) or any parameter is `422 validation_error`, a blank content identifier is `422 validation_error`, and an unknown identifier is `404 content_not_found` — all validation completes before any lookup. The success body is compact UTF-8 JSON terminated by exactly one newline, with members in exactly the order `content_id`, `claim_count`, `bundle_count`, `attestation_count`, `qualified_signer_count`, `coverage_status`. `content_id` echoes the requested identifier; every count is an integer. `claim_count` covers only the existing claims that directly assert this exact content; `bundle_count` covers the distinct existing evidence bundles attached to those claims, deduplicated in stable creation order; `attestation_count` covers the existing attestations whose target is one of those claims or bundles, retaining revoked proofs; `qualified_signer_count` is the number of distinct signing actors with a verified, non-revoked attestation of any of those targets (an actor whose proofs are all revoked counts as zero). `coverage_status` is exactly `uncovered` when the content has no claims (all counts zero), `partial` when it has claims but no qualified signer, and `covered` once at least one qualified signer exists — the summary never changes the existing trust-evaluation thresholds. The read touches only contents, claims, evidence bundles, attestations, and revocations; it writes no resource, snapshot, audit event, or log, and raw content, claim payloads, evidence bytes, raw signatures, and private keys never enter the response, persistence, or logs. Repeated reads and reads across an app restart return the same counts and status for the same persisted state.
- `GET /v1/content-coverage-search?actor_id=...&media_type=...&coverage_status=...&limit=...&cursor=...` — read-only reviewer cross-content evidence-coverage search, the cross-content counterpart of the single-content summary above. The request body must be empty: carrying any bytes (even whitespace or malformed JSON) is `422 validation_error`, rejected before any parameter or content is read. The success body is compact UTF-8 JSON (compact separators, unescaped non-ASCII) terminated by exactly one newline, with members in exactly the order `items`, `count`, `next_cursor`; each item is exactly the existing content public view (`id`, `digest_algorithm`, `digest_hex`, `media_type`, `title`, `actor_id`, UTC `created_at`) followed by the four existing coverage counts and the coverage status (`claim_count`, `bundle_count`, `attestation_count`, `qualified_signer_count`, `coverage_status`) computed under exactly the single-content summary rules — direct claims only, their distinct bundles, attestations of those claims or bundles with revoked proofs retained, and distinct verified non-revoked signing actors — and no other field is ever added. Items follow the contents' stable creation order (`created_at`, with the persistent insertion order as a same-timestamp tiebreaker that survives a restart). Optional `actor_id` and `media_type` are non-empty, case/whitespace-sensitive exact matches that combine as logical AND (absent means unfiltered); they are never resolved for existence, so an unknown or nonexistent value is an empty collection, not a 404. `coverage_status` accepts only the three existing coverage literals `uncovered`, `partial`, `covered` (case-sensitive; blank, capitalized, or any other spelling is `422`, never normalized) and keeps only contents whose computed status equals it. `count` is the filtered total covering every page, independent of the page returned. `limit` is a pure decimal integer from 1 to 100 defaulting to 50; `cursor` is an opaque HMAC-signed server token in its own `cc1` family, bound to every effective filter (including `null` filters) and the effective limit, so continuation pages repeat and omit nothing, the final page carries `next_cursor: null`, and a cursor at or past the tail returns empty `items` with the original `count` and `null`. The first page carries no `cursor`; a continuation carries the previous response's `next_cursor` with the same query conditions. Blank/illegal/repeated/undeclared parameters and an empty, whitespace-only, malformed, tampered, cross-family/foreign, or query-mismatching `cursor` are all `422 validation_error` — nothing is silently defaulted or normalized. No match is an empty collection (`{"items": [], "count": 0, "next_cursor": null}`). Success, empty results, and failures are strictly read-only (no content, resource, or audit event is created or modified), and no claim payload, raw signature, private key, content bytes, or evidence bytes ever enter the response. Non-`GET` methods on this route are rejected with `405 method_not_allowed`.
- `GET /v1/evidence-bundles/{evidence_bundle_id}/exchange` — read-only evidence-bundle interoperability snapshot for external verifiers. The success body is exactly `{"content", "claim", "evidence_bundle", "attestations"}`: `content` is the full public view of the content the bundle's directly associated claim asserts, `claim` is the full public view of the single claim the bundle is directly attached to, `evidence_bundle` is the bundle's existing full public view, and `attestations` lists only the existing attestations whose target type is `evidence_bundle` and whose target id equals this bundle, in stable creation order, each with exactly the existing attestation detail fields (a revoked attestation is retained so the snapshot stays historically auditable). The content graph is never expanded through lineage and no other content, claim, bundle, or attestation is ever included; the raw signature, claim payload, content bytes, and evidence bytes are neither stored nor echoed. A bundle with no attestations yields `"attestations": []`. The route accepts no query parameters — any parameter or repeated parameter is `422 validation_error` — and an unknown evidence bundle id is the existing `404 evidence_bundle_not_found`. Success, empty attestation lists, and failures create no resource, modify no record, and add no audit event.
- `GET /v1/evidence-bundles/{evidence_bundle_id}/exchange/manifest` — read-only integrity manifest for the exchange snapshot above. The success body is exactly `{"manifest_version", "evidence_bundle_id", "digest_algorithm", "manifest_digest_hex"}`: `manifest_version` is fixed at `provenance-exchange-manifest-v1` and `digest_algorithm` is fixed at `sha256`. `manifest_digest_hex` is the SHA-256 hex digest of the canonical JSON object built from exactly the snapshot's `content`, `claim`, `evidence_bundle`, and `attestations` members: the root member names and array element order are kept exactly as in the snapshot, nested object members are ordered by Unicode code point, and serialization uses compact separators, unescaped non-ASCII characters, and UTF-8 encoding. No other resource, internal sequence number, raw signature, claim payload, content bytes, or evidence bytes participate in the digest; a revoked attestation is not removed from the snapshot and therefore still contributes. The same persisted state always yields the same manifest on repeated reads (including across an app restart). The route accepts no query parameters — any parameter or repeated parameter is `422 validation_error`, validated before the bundle lookup — and an unknown evidence bundle id is the existing `404 evidence_bundle_not_found`. Reads and failures create no resource, modify no record, and add no audit event; the existing snapshot, identifiers, UTC fields, and error JSON are unchanged.
- `GET /v1/evidence-bundles/{evidence_bundle_id}/exchange/package` — read-only one-call export of the exchange snapshot together with its integrity manifest. The success body is exactly `{"snapshot", "manifest"}`: `snapshot` is exactly the four-member body of the existing `GET .../exchange` route (`content`, `claim`, `evidence_bundle`, `attestations`, each the existing public view), and `manifest` is exactly the four-field body of the existing `GET .../exchange/manifest` route. The manifest digest is computed over exactly the `snapshot` member returned in the same response under the existing canonical rules (root members and array element order kept, nested object keys sorted by Unicode code point, compact separators, unescaped non-ASCII, UTF-8), and both halves derive from a single snapshot read, so they are always mutually consistent. No lineage is traversed and no other resource, internal sequence number, raw signature, claim payload, content bytes, or evidence bytes are included; a bundle with no attestations yields `"attestations": []` with the digest computed over that empty array. The route accepts no query parameters — any parameter or repeated parameter is `422 validation_error`, validated before the bundle lookup — and an unknown evidence bundle id is the existing `404 evidence_bundle_not_found`. Success, empty attestation lists, and failures create no resource, modify no record, and add no audit event; repeated reads and reads across an app restart return the same package, and the existing exchange route, manifest route, identifiers, UTC fields, and error JSON are unchanged.
- `POST /v1/exchange-manifest-verifications` — stateless offline verification of a received exchange snapshot against its integrity manifest, for third-party verifiers. The request body is exactly `{"manifest_version", "evidence_bundle_id", "digest_algorithm", "manifest_digest_hex", "snapshot"}`: `manifest_version` must be `provenance-exchange-manifest-v1`, `digest_algorithm` must be `sha256`, and `manifest_digest_hex` must be exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. `snapshot` is exactly `{"content", "claim", "evidence_bundle", "attestations"}` whose nested objects carry exactly the existing public-view fields; `evidence_bundle.id` must equal the manifest's `evidence_bundle_id`, `claim.id` must equal `evidence_bundle.claim_id`, `content.id` must equal `claim.content_id`, and every attestation must have `target_type: "evidence_bundle"` with `target_id` equal to the manifest's bundle id. The snapshot is canonicalized under the existing manifest rules (root members and array elements keep their received order, nested object members sort by Unicode code point, compact separators, unescaped non-ASCII, UTF-8) and hashed with SHA-256. Any structural, field, association, or raw-material violation is `422 validation_error`; a structurally valid request whose computed digest differs is `200 {"valid": false, "computed_digest_hex": ...}`, and a match is exactly `{"valid": true}`. The route is purely a function of the request body: it never queries, creates, or modifies any local resource or audit record, so unknown bundle ids verify exactly like known ones.
- `POST /v1/evidence-bundle-exchange-imports` — controlled registration of an exchange package already received and verified offline, for an external forensics system. The request body is exactly `{"manifest", "snapshot"}`: `manifest` is the existing four-field exchange manifest (`manifest_version`, `evidence_bundle_id`, `digest_algorithm`, `manifest_digest_hex`) and `snapshot` is the existing four-member exchange snapshot (`content`, `claim`, `evidence_bundle`, `attestations`), both validated exactly as on the stateless verification route — fixed `provenance-exchange-manifest-v1` version and `sha256` algorithm, a 64-lowercase-hex manifest digest, existing public-view fields only, and the same internal associations (bundle id matches the manifest, the claim matches the bundle, the content matches the claim, every attestation targets this exact bundle). The snapshot is canonicalized under the existing manifest rules over the raw received JSON (root member and array order kept, nested object keys sorted by Unicode code point, compact separators, unescaped non-ASCII, UTF-8) and hashed with SHA-256; the computed digest must equal the manifest's claimed digest. Verification is decided by the request body alone and never resolves any identifier against local resources, so whether the referenced content, claim, bundle, or attestations exist locally cannot change the verdict, and no such resource is created. No field can carry a raw signature, claim payload, content bytes, or evidence bytes: undeclared fields on any member are rejected. Missing or extra top-level fields, malformed JSON, and every structural, field, association, raw-material, or digest-mismatch failure are `422 validation_error` and write nothing. On success the receiving identity is exactly `(manifest_version, evidence_bundle_id, manifest_digest_hex)`; the first submission returns `201` with a stable deterministic `eir_` receipt id, the three identity fields, and a UTC `received_at`, and writes the receipt row together with the `evidence_bundle.exchange_imported` audit event in a single transaction. A retry for the same identity returns `200` with the original receipt (including its original `received_at`) and writes no second row or audit event — even when the retried snapshot itself no longer matches, in which case the retry is `422` and the original record is untouched. The full snapshot is never copied or persisted: the receipt holds only the identity fields.
- `GET /v1/evidence-bundle-exchange-imports/{import_id}` — read the public receipt for one registered exchange import: exactly `{"id", "manifest_version", "evidence_bundle_id", "manifest_digest_hex", "received_at"}`, with `received_at` a UTC timestamp. The snapshot and every raw material are never returned. An unknown id is an explicit `404 evidence_bundle_exchange_import_not_found` carrying the requested `import_id`; the read is strictly read-only and writes no resource or audit event.
- `GET /v1/evidence-bundle-exchange-imports?manifest_version=...&evidence_bundle_id=...&manifest_digest_hex=...&limit=...&cursor=...` — read-only search over existing exchange-import receipts. The success body is exactly `{"items", "count", "next_cursor"}`; each item is the existing single-receipt public view (`id`, `manifest_version`, `evidence_bundle_id`, `manifest_digest_hex`, UTC `received_at`; the snapshot is never returned) in stable creation order (`created_at` with the monotonic `seq` tiebreaker). Optional `manifest_version`, `evidence_bundle_id`, and `manifest_digest_hex` are non-empty, case- and whitespace-sensitive exact matches that combine as logical AND; absent means unfiltered. `count` is the filtered total, independent of the page. `limit` is a decimal integer from 1 to 100 defaulting to 50; `cursor` is an opaque HMAC-signed server token that binds to every effective filter and the limit, so pages resume without duplication or omission and the final page carries `next_cursor: null` (a cursor at or past the end returns an empty page with the total `count`). Blank/illegal/repeated/undeclared parameters and an empty, malformed, tampered, foreign-family, or query-mismatching `cursor` are `422 validation_error` — nothing is silently normalized or defaulted — and no match is an empty collection (`{"items": [], "count": 0, "next_cursor": null}`). The search is strictly read-only: it writes no resource and no audit event.
- `GET /v1/evidence-bundle-exchange-imports/{import_id}/reconciliation` — read-only reconciliation of one registered exchange-import receipt against current local state. The receipt is read by `import_id`; an unknown id is the existing `404 evidence_bundle_exchange_import_not_found`. The success body is exactly `{"import_id", "local_available", "local_manifest_digest_hex", "matches"}`. The receipt's `evidence_bundle_id` is the only local lookup key — the bundle is resolved by that id alone, never by a reverse digest or receipt search — and when no local bundle has that id the body is `(receipt id, false, null, false)` with a `200`. When a local bundle exists, `local_available` is `true` and `local_manifest_digest_hex` is the bundle's current digest computed under exactly the `GET /v1/evidence-bundles/{evidence_bundle_id}/exchange/manifest` rules; `matches` is `true` only when that digest equals the receipt's `manifest_digest_hex` character for character, otherwise `false`. The route accepts no query parameters — any parameter or repeated parameter is `422 validation_error`, validated before the receipt lookup. The snapshot, raw signatures, payloads, and bytes are never echoed; the read is strictly read-only and writes no resource, receipt, or audit event, and the existing error JSON, identifiers, and UTC fields are unchanged.
- `GET /v1/evidence-bundle-exchange-import-reconciliations?local_available=...&matches=...&limit=...&cursor=...` — read-only, paginated reconciliation of every existing exchange-import receipt against current local state. Only `local_available`, `matches`, `limit`, and `cursor` are accepted: any unknown, repeated, blank, or illegal parameter is `422 validation_error`. The success body is strictly `{"items", "count", "next_cursor"}`; receipts are returned in the same stable creation order (`created_at` with the monotonic `seq` tiebreaker), filtered items keep that order, and `count` is the total number of receipts matching the active filters, independent of the page. Each item is the existing single-receipt public view (`id`, `manifest_version`, `evidence_bundle_id`, `manifest_digest_hex`, UTC `received_at`) plus `local_available`, `local_manifest_digest_hex`, and `matches`; each item is reconciled using only its own `evidence_bundle_id` under exactly the single-receipt reconciliation rules — no local bundle gives `false`/`null`/`false`; when a local bundle exists its current exchange manifest digest is reported and `matches` is `true` only on character-for-character equality with the receipt digest. The optional `local_available` and `matches` filters are each provided at most once and accept only the lowercase literals `true` or `false` (blank, capitalized, numeric, or other spellings are `422`); an absent filter imposes no restriction and the two combine as logical AND against the fields computed at that read (there is no reverse lookup by digest or any other resource). Note that `matches=false` keeps both unavailable and available-but-diverged receipts, while `local_available=false&matches=true` can never match and is therefore a 200 empty collection. `limit` is a decimal integer from 1 to 100 defaulting to 50; `cursor` is an opaque HMAC-signed server token (its own `ir1` family) binding to both effective filters (`null` when unfiltered) and the effective limit, so pages resume without duplication or omission and the final page carries `next_cursor: null` (a cursor at or past the end of the filtered set returns an empty page with the filtered `count`; an empty, malformed, tampered, foreign-family, or filter/limit-mismatching cursor is `422 validation_error`). Parameters and the cursor are all validated before any receipt or local bundle is read; no matching receipts is an empty collection (`{"items": [], "count": 0, "next_cursor": null}`). The snapshot, raw signatures, payloads, and bytes are never echoed; the route is strictly read-only and writes no resource, receipt, or audit event on success or failure, and it is compatible with the existing single-receipt reconciliation, the unfiltered collection behavior, and the error JSON.

The first bundle creation and its `evidence_bundle.created` audit event commit in a single transaction. Blank text fields, non-object metadata, unsupported algorithms or malformed digests, malformed JSON, and **any undeclared request field** are `422 validation_error`; an unknown claim on creation or listing remains `404 claim_not_found`. In particular, fields that could carry raw evidence (for example `data` or `evidence`) are not silently ignored: they are rejected with `422` and write neither a resource nor an audit event.

## Asynchronous content export jobs

An export job is a server-tracked, runnable resource that produces the read-only content provenance-evidence snapshot (see `GET /v1/contents/{content_id}/export`) asynchronously. Jobs are append-oriented: each moves monotonically through `pending` → `running` → `succeeded`/`failed`, and a settled or in-flight job can never be claimed or run again. The `request_id` is a client-supplied idempotency key.

- `POST /v1/content-export-jobs` — body contains exactly an existing non-empty `content_id` and a non-empty client-supplied `request_id` (surrounding whitespace is trimmed); any undeclared field is rejected. The first submission returns `201` with exactly `{id, content_id, request_id, status, created_at, started_at, finished_at, result, error}` — a stable deterministic `cxj_` id, `status: "pending"`, a timezone-aware UTC `created_at`, and `started_at`, `finished_at`, `result`, and `error` all `null` — and writes the job row together with the `content_export_job.created` audit event in a single transaction. A retried submission for the same `(request_id, content_id)` returns `200` with the original job in whatever its current lifecycle state is and writes no second row or audit event. Reusing the same `request_id` for a *different* `content_id` is `409 content_export_request_conflict` and writes nothing. Missing/blank/whitespace fields, wrong-typed or null values, malformed JSON, and undeclared fields are `422 validation_error`; an unknown content id is `404 content_not_found`.
- `GET /v1/content-export-jobs/{job_id}` — returns one job's public view with exactly the nine fields above, or `404 content_export_job_not_found` (whose details carry the requested `job_id`). The read is strictly read-only: it writes no job and no audit event.
- `GET /v1/content-export-jobs?content_id=...&request_id=...&status=...&from=...&to=...&limit=...&cursor=...` — read-only cross-job search over existing content export jobs. The request body must be empty: carrying any body is `422 validation_error`, rejected before any parameter or job is read. The success body is exactly `{"items", "count", "next_cursor"}`; each item is the existing single-job public view (the nine fields above, including a settled job's `result` snapshot, which itself carries only the existing public views — never raw content, claim payloads, or evidence bytes), and items follow the jobs' stable creation order (`created_at` with the monotonic `seq` tiebreaker). Optional `content_id`, `request_id`, and `status` combine as logical AND; `content_id`/`request_id` are non-empty, case/whitespace-sensitive exact matches (absent means unfiltered) and are never resolved for existence — an unknown content or request id is an empty collection, not an error. `status` accepts only the four existing lifecycle literals `pending`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed` (case-sensitive; blank, capitalized, or any other spelling is `422`, never normalized), and absent means no status filtering. `from` and `to` are strict RFC 3339 UTC instants (`Z` or `+00:00`) applied as inclusive `created_at` bounds, and `from` must not be later than `to`. `count` is the filtered total covering every page, independent of the page returned. `limit` is a pure decimal integer from 1 to 100 defaulting to 50 (no sign, decimal point, or whitespace); `cursor` is an opaque HMAC-signed server token in its own `cx1` family, bound to every effective filter (including `null` filters) and the effective limit, so pages resume without duplication or omission, replay the same page when reused, and the final page carries `next_cursor: null` (a cursor at or past the tail returns an empty page with the same filtered `count`). Empty/blank/illegal/repeated/undeclared parameters, a `from` later than `to`, and an empty, whitespace-only, malformed, tampered, wrong-signature, cross-endpoint/foreign-family, or filter/limit-mismatching `cursor` are all `422 validation_error` — parameters and the cursor are validated before any job is read and nothing is silently defaulted. No match returns `{"items": [], "count": 0, "next_cursor": null}`. The success body is compact UTF-8 JSON (compact separators, unescaped non-ASCII) terminated by exactly one newline; timestamps stay UTC, booleans and `null` are rendered as such, and all numbers are integral (no `-0.0` or non-finite values). Each read mints a fresh opaque cursor; the search is strictly read-only — it creates no job, changes no state, writes no audit event, and never returns attachments or raw content, payload, or evidence bytes. Job status may change between queries while ids and creation order stay stable, so the same status filter recomputes consistently across a restart.
- `POST /v1/content-export-jobs/{job_id}/run` — atomically claims a `pending` job and runs it to completion in one transaction. The `pending → running` transition is a single conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE status = 'pending'` that stamps a timezone-aware UTC `started_at`, so of concurrent or repeated calls exactly one claims the job and any other — a concurrent loser, or a repeat call once the job has settled — returns `409 conflict` without changing state or writing an audit event. The winning run builds the existing read-only content export and settles exactly once: on success it returns `200` with `status: "succeeded"`, a timezone-aware UTC `finished_at`, `error: null`, and `result` equal to the body of `GET /v1/contents/{content_id}/export` (exactly `{"content", "claims"}`, claims for this content only in stable order each with its evidence bundles); if the export raises, it returns `200` with `status: "failed"`, a UTC `finished_at`, `result: null`, and `error: "content_export_failed"`. Either settlement records the `content_export_job.run` audit event in the same transaction, so the job is never left stuck in `running`. An unknown job id is `404 content_export_job_not_found`. The run never traverses lineage, never mutates any content/claim/bundle, and its `result` carries only the existing public views — never raw content, claim payloads, or evidence bytes.
- `POST /v1/content-export-jobs/run-next` — server-side queue claim: selects the single oldest `pending` job in the same stable creation order (`created_at` with the monotonic `seq` tiebreaker, which stays stable across an app restart) and immediately performs exactly one atomic run under the single-job run semantics above. The request body must be empty and the route accepts no query parameters: any non-empty body (including whitespace, malformed JSON, a JSON object, or any extra field) and any query parameter (including a blank or repeated parameter) is `422 validation_error`, rejected before any job is read. When at least one job is pending it returns `200` with the claimed job's complete nine-field public view: success settles `succeeded` with UTC `started_at`/`finished_at` and `result` identical to the existing content export snapshot; an export that raises settles `failed` with UTC `finished_at`, `result: null`, and `error: "content_export_failed"` (still `200`); either settlement writes the `content_export_job.run` audit event in the same transaction. Only the oldest pending job is claimed — every other pending job, including younger jobs, remains queued unchanged — and a second call then claims the next oldest. When no job is pending it returns `404 content_export_job_not_found` with zero writes (no job, resource, or audit row). The claim uses the same conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE status = 'pending'` as the single-job run, so of concurrent calls at most one wins any given job: a concurrent loser that picked the same oldest job before it was claimed gets `409 conflict` without modifying any job, creating any resource, or writing an audit event, and it never falls through to a younger queued job. The route never traverses lineage, changes the export snapshot's fields/order/UTC/error JSON, or alters job creation, detail, single-job run, idempotent retry, or `request_id` conflict semantics.
- `GET /v1/content-export-jobs/summary` — read-only queue summary over all existing content export jobs. The request body must be empty and the route accepts no query parameters: any non-empty body (including whitespace, malformed JSON, a JSON object, or any extra field) and any query parameter (unknown, blank, or repeated) is `422 validation_error`, and both validations complete before any job is read, so an invalid request never produces a partial summary. The success body is exactly `{"pending", "running", "succeeded", "failed", "oldest_pending_id", "oldest_pending_wait_seconds"}`: the four counts cover every existing job keyed by its current lifecycle state (settled jobs remain in their `succeeded`/`failed` counts), computed from the current persisted state at read time; `oldest_pending_id` is the stable id of the single oldest `pending` job in the stable creation order (`created_at` with the monotonic `seq` tiebreaker), and `oldest_pending_wait_seconds` is the current UTC instant minus that job's `created_at`, floored to whole integer seconds. On an empty queue every count is zero and both oldest-pending members are `null`. The success body is compact UTF-8 JSON (compact separators, unescaped non-ASCII) terminated by exactly one newline; all numbers are integral (no `-0.0` or non-finite values). 112	## Asynchronous audit checkpoint export jobs
113	
114	An audit checkpoint job is a server-tracked, runnable resource that produces the read-only filtered audit-event checkpoint package (see `GET /v1/audit-events/checkpoint/package`) asynchronously. Jobs are append-oriented: each moves monotonically through `pending` → `running` → `succeeded`/`failed`, and a settled or in-flight job can never be claimed or run again. The `request_id` is a client-supplied idempotency key.
115	
116	- `POST /v1/audit-checkpoint-jobs` — body contains exactly a non-empty `request_id` and the four audit-checkpoint filters (`event_type`/`resource_id` exact matches, strict UTC `from`/`to` bounds, each null when unfiltered); any undeclared field or query parameter is `422 validation_error`. The first submission returns `201` with a stable deterministic `acj_` id, `status: "pending"`, a timezone-aware UTC `created_at`, and null `started_at`/`finished_at`/`result`/`error`, writing the job row together with the `audit_checkpoint_job.created` audit event in a single transaction. A retried submission for the same `request_id` and the same effective filter returns `200` with the original job; the same `request_id` with a different filter is `409 audit_checkpoint_request_conflict` with zero writes.
117	- `GET /v1/audit-checkpoint-jobs/{job_id}` — returns one job's public view, or `404 audit_checkpoint_job_not_found`. The read is strictly read-only and writes no job or audit event.
118	- `POST /v1/audit-checkpoint-jobs/{job_id}/run` and `POST /v1/audit-checkpoint-jobs/run-next` — atomically claim a `pending` job (a single conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE status = 'pending'` stamping a timezone-aware UTC `started_at`) and settle it exactly once: `succeeded` with a UTC `finished_at` and a `result` equal to the checkpoint package for the job's filter, or `failed` with UTC `started_at` and `finished_at`, `result: null`, and `error: "audit_checkpoint_export_failed"`, recording the `audit_checkpoint_job.run` audit event in the same transaction. A non-pending, concurrent, or repeated run is `409 conflict` with zero writes; `run-next` claims only the single oldest pending job in stable creation order and returns `404 audit_checkpoint_job_not_found` when the queue is empty.
119	- `GET /v1/audit-checkpoint-jobs/summary` — read-only queue summary over all existing audit checkpoint jobs, for judging pending volume and settlement. The request is exactly an empty `GET`: it takes no body and no query parameters. Any request-body bytes (whitespace, arbitrary bytes, malformed JSON, or a non-empty body such as a JSON object) and any unknown, blank, undeclared, or repeated query parameter are `422 validation_error`, and both validations complete before any job is read, so an invalid request is rejected first and never produces a partial summary. Non-`GET` methods are `405 method_not_allowed`. The success body is compact UTF-8 JSON (compact separators, unescaped non-ASCII) terminated by exactly one newline, with members in exactly the order `{"pending", "running", "succeeded", "failed", "oldest_pending_id", "oldest_pending_wait_seconds"}`: the four counts cover every existing job keyed by its current persisted lifecycle state (settled jobs remain in their `succeeded`/`failed` counts), computed from the current persisted state at read time; `oldest_pending_id` is the stable id of the single oldest `pending` job from the business-object view, chosen in stable creation order (`created_at` with the monotonic `seq` tiebreaker), an identifier stable across an app restart; and `oldest_pending_wait_seconds` is the current UTC instant minus that job's `created_at`, floored to whole integer seconds. On an empty queue (or when no job is pending) every count is zero and both oldest-pending members are `null`. Times stay UTC; every rendered number is an integer, and the JSON never contains negative zero or a non-finite value. If the database is unreadable or the summary query fails internally, the route returns `503 service_unavailable` under the existing `{"error": {"code", "message", "details"}}` structure with a machine-readable `details.reason` (`database_unavailable` or `internal_error`), never a partial body; the failed read rolls back and writes nothing. A successful read, an empty queue, and every failed request create, modify, or delete no job, resource, or audit event, and the route returns no raw material — no filter, checkpoint, event, result, or payload; the settled view stays consistent with the checkpoint and events served by the audit checkpoint package under the same filter. It freezes nothing: job status may change between reads, while the same persisted state read across an app restart returns the same counts and the same stable oldest id, with the wait time recomputed at each read's own instant. Job creation, detail, single-job run, queue claim, idempotent conflict, and audit-event write semantics are unchanged.
120	
121	## Verifiable attestations
122	
123	Attestations cryptographically bind an existing signing actor to an existing claim or evidence bundle. They only associate targets that already exist; they never create claims, bundles, or actors. The service verifies Ed25519 signatures but never holds a private key, and only verified attestations are ever written.
124	
125	- `POST /v1/attestations` — body contains `target_type` (`"claim"` or `"evidence_bundle"`), the existing `target_id`, an existing `signer_actor_id`, a Base64 Ed25519 `public_key` that decodes to exactly **32 bytes**, and a Base64 `signature` that decodes to exactly **64 bytes**. The signature is verified against the exact UTF-8 canonical JSON array (compact separators, non-ASCII emitted unescaped):
126	
127	  ```
128	  ["provenance-attestation-v1",target_type,target_id,signer_actor_id]
129	  ```
130	
131	  A signature over any other serialization (reordered elements, whitespace, ASCII `\u` escapes, a different prefix/actor) fails verification. The first creation returns `201` with the stable `att_` id, `target_type`/`target_id`, `signer_actor_id`, the Base64 public key, the `sha256` hex digest of the signature, `verified: true`, and a UTC `created_at`. The raw signature is never persisted or echoed — only its SHA-256 digest is stored. A repeat submission with the same target, signing actor, public key, and signature digest returns `200` with the existing attestation and writes no row or audit event.
132	- `GET /v1/attestations/{attestation_id}` — full public fields, or `404 attestation_not_found`.
133	- `GET /v1/attestations?target_type=...&target_id=...` — all attestations in stable creation order as `{"items", "count"}`, optionally filtered by `target_type` (`claim` / `evidence_bundle`; any other value is `422 validation_error`) and/or `target_id`. Filtering is an empty collection (`{"items": [], "count": 0}`), never a 404.
134	
135	The first attestation write and its `attestation.created` audit event commit in a single transaction. An unknown target is `404 claim_not_found` / `evidence_bundle_not_found` (matched by the declared `target_type`), and an unknown signing actor is `404 unknown_actor` even when the signature itself is valid. Bad Base64, wrong decoded lengths (32/64 bytes), blank identifiers, unknown `target_type`, undeclared fields, and malformed JSON are `422 validation_error`; a well-formed request whose signature fails verification is `422 attestation_verification_failed`, with no resource or audit write. Signature verification uses an RFC 8032 Ed25519 implementation in the Python standard library (no external crypto dependency).
136	
137	## Trust evaluation for reviewers
138	
139	Reviewers can ask the service to evaluate how many independent signing subjects have verified a given claim or evidence bundle. The evaluation is purely read-only: it computes its answer from the attestations already stored and creates neither a resource nor an audit event.
140	
141	- `GET /v1/trust-evaluations?target_type=claim|evidence_bundle&target_id=...&min_signers=...` — `target_type` is required and must be exactly `claim` or `evidence_bundle`; `target_id` is required and non-blank. `min_signers` is optional and must be a plain decimal integer from 1 to 100, defaulting to 1 (no sign, decimal point, or leading/trailing whitespace). Returns exactly `{"target_type", "target_id", "min_signers", "qualified_signer_count", "decision"}`. Only attestations of the exact target with `verified=true` and **no recorded revocation** are counted (every stored attestation is a verified one, but a revoked attestation is retained for history yet no longer qualifies), and the count is the number of **distinct** `signer_actor_id` values: several attestations by the same actor — for example under different keys — qualify once. If a signer's only attestation of the target is revoked, that actor drops out of the count; a target whose attestations are all revoked evaluates like one with no attestations. `decision` is `trusted` when `qualified_signer_count >= min_signers` and `untrusted` otherwise (an existing target with no qualifying attestations evaluates to zero signers and `untrusted`, not to a 404). The result is computed live on every request. Parameters are fully validated before any existence lookup: missing/blank/unknown/repeated `target_type` or `target_id`, a blank identifier, an undeclared parameter, and a non-integer, out-of-range, signed, or whitespace-bearing `min_signers` are all `422 validation_error` — nothing is silently defaulted or normalized. Once the parameters are valid, a missing target is `404 claim_not_found` or `404 evidence_bundle_not_found` according to the declared `target_type` (declaring an existing bundle's id as a claim, or vice versa, is likewise a 404).
142	
143	## Immutable attestation revocations
144	
145	A revocation is an immutable, append-only record that an existing attestation is no longer relied upon. It neither updates nor deletes the attestation: the original proof and its `attestation.created` audit relationship are preserved. There is deliberately no update or delete path for a revocation.
146	
147	- `POST /v1/attestation-revocations` — body contains the existing `attestation_id`, an existing `revoker_actor_id` (which need not be the attestation's signer), and a non-empty `reason` (surrounding whitespace is trimmed). The first creation returns `201` with the stable `rev_` id, the `attestation_id`/`revoker_actor_id` associations, the reason, and a UTC `created_at`. A repeat submission of the same attestation, revoking actor, and reason returns `200` with the existing record and adds no row or audit event; any different combination (a different revoker or a different reason) forms an independent record that is separately retained. Revocations never accept, store, or echo the original signature.
148	- `GET /v1/attestation-revocations/{revocation_id}` — full public fields, or `404 attestation_revocation_not_found`.
149	- `GET /v1/attestations/{attestation_id}/revocations` — that attestation's revocation records only, in stable creation order as `{"items", "count"}`; an unknown attestation id is `404 attestation_not_found` (a missing attestation is never an empty collection).
150	- `GET /v1/attestation-revocations?attestation_id=...&revoker_actor_id=...&reason=...&from=...&to=...&limit=...&cursor=...` — global read-only search across every proof's immutable revocation records. Returns `{"items", "count", "next_cursor"}` where each item reuses the single-revocation public view (`id`, `attestation_id`, `revoker_actor_id`, `reason`, UTC `created_at`); the proof payload, signatures, authentication headers, private keys, and content bytes are never returned. Records are returned in stable creation order (`created_at`, with the persistence insertion order breaking same-instant ties, stable across restarts). Optional `attestation_id`, `revoker_actor_id`, and `reason` are non-empty, case/whitespace-sensitive exact matches that combine as logical AND — an unknown value yields an empty collection, never a 404; `from` and `to` are strict RFC 3339 UTC instants applied as inclusive `created_at` bounds, and `from` must not be later than `to`. `limit` is a pure decimal integer from 1 to 100 defaulting to 50; `cursor` is an opaque HMAC-signed server token (its own `ar1` family) binding to every effective filter and the limit, so pages resume without duplication or omission, `count` is always the filtered total across all pages, the first page carries no cursor, and the final and past-the-tail pages carry `next_cursor: null` with an empty page at or past the tail. Blank, wrong-typed, malformed, out-of-range, repeated, or undeclared parameters; a `from` later than `to`; an empty, malformed, tampered, foreign-family, or filter/limit-mismatching `cursor`; and any non-empty request body (whitespace, arbitrary bytes, or bad JSON included) are all `422 validation_error`, validated before any revocation record is read and never returning partial results. No matching records yields an empty collection. Success, empty results, and failures are strictly read-only: no revocation, grant, or audit event is created, modified, or deleted; revocation creation idempotency, transactions, append history, and access authorization are unchanged.
151	
152	The first revocation write and its `attestation.revoked` audit event commit in a single transaction. An unknown attestation is `404 attestation_not_found` and an unknown revoking actor is `404 unknown_actor`. Blank or whitespace-only `attestation_id`, `revoker_actor_id`, or `reason`, malformed JSON, and any undeclared request field are `422 validation_error` and write neither a record nor an audit event. Because records are append-only, any attempt to update or delete a revocation is met with `405 method_not_allowed`; no such mutation path is provided.
153	
154	## Cross-content revocation impact search
155	
156	Reviewers can read, in one read-only query, what each existing revocation means for the evidence coverage of the content its revoked proof belongs to. The endpoint is the cross-content counterpart of the single-content evidence-coverage summary and is strictly read-only.
157	
158	- `GET /v1/revocation-impacts?attestation_id=...&revoker_actor_id=...&reason=...&from=...&to=...&limit=...&cursor=...` — read-only cross-content impact search across every existing attestation revocation. The request carries no body: any body bytes (even whitespace, arbitrary bytes, or malformed JSON) are `422 validation_error`, rejected before any query parameter, cursor, or revocation record is read. The success body is compact UTF-8 JSON (compact separators, unescaped non-ASCII) terminated by exactly one newline, with members in exactly the order `items`, `count`, `next_cursor`. Each item corresponds to one existing revocation record and reuses the existing revocation public view (`id`, `attestation_id`, `revoker_actor_id`, `reason`, UTC `created_at`), followed by exactly `content_id`, `target_type`, `signer_actor_id`, `qualified_signer_count_after`, `coverage_status_after`, `qualified_signer_count_before`, `coverage_status_before`, and `qualified_signer_count_delta`. `content_id` is the content the revoked proof's target belongs to — the claim's content for a `claim` target, and the content of the bundle's claim for an `evidence_bundle` target; `target_type` is the revoked attestation's target type (`claim` or `evidence_bundle`) and `signer_actor_id` is its signing subject. The after/before qualified-signer counts both follow exactly the single-content evidence-coverage summary caliber: the number of distinct signing actors with a verified, non-revoked attestation of a claim directly asserting the content or a distinct bundle attached to such a claim, counted per independent subject. The **after** counts apply every stored revocation; the **before** counts ignore only that item's own revocation while every other revocation remains in force, so `qualified_signer_count_delta = before - after` is always exactly `0` or `1`. `coverage_status_before`/`coverage_status_after` use only the three existing literals `uncovered`, `partial`, and `covered` under the same rules as the summary (no claims → `uncovered`; claims but no qualified signer → `partial`; at least one qualified signer → `covered`), and therefore reflect the change the revocation made to that content's coverage. Items are returned in the revocations' stable creation order (`created_at`, with the persistent insertion order as a same-timestamp tiebreaker that survives a restart), and every `created_at` stays timezone-aware UTC. Optional `attestation_id`, `revoker_actor_id`, and `reason` are non-empty, case/whitespace-sensitive exact matches, each provided at most once, that combine as logical AND (absent means unfiltered); filter values are never resolved for existence, so an unknown or nonexistent value is an empty collection rather than a missing-resource error. `from` and `to` are strict RFC 3339 UTC instants (`Z` or `+00:00`, seconds required, no naive or non-UTC value), each provided at most once and applied as inclusive `created_at` bounds; a `from` later than `to` is `422 validation_error`. `count` is the filtered total covering every page, independent of the page returned. `limit` is a pure decimal integer from 1 to 100 defaulting to 50 (no sign, decimal point, exponent, or whitespace); `cursor` is an opaque HMAC-signed server token in its own `ri1` family, bound to every effective filter (including `null` filters; the time claim canonicalizes equivalent `Z` and `+00:00` spellings to the same instant) and the effective limit, so continuation pages repeat and omit nothing, replaying a cursor returns the same page, the final page carries `next_cursor: null`, a cursor at or past the tail returns empty `items` with the original `count` and `null`, and a query with no match returns `{"items": [], "count": 0, "next_cursor": null}`. The first page carries no `cursor`; a continuation carries the previous response's `next_cursor` with the same query conditions. Blank/illegal/repeated/undeclared parameters, an empty/whitespace-only/malformed/tampered/cross-family (including the `ar1` revocation-list family)/foreign/filter-or-limit-mismatching `cursor`, and any non-empty request body are all `422 validation_error` — parameters and the cursor are validated before any revocation is read and nothing is silently defaulted or normalized. Every count renders as an integer (no negative zero) and the response never contains the raw signature, signature digest, public key, claim payload, content bytes, or evidence bytes. The search is strictly read-only: success, empty results, and failures create or modify no revocation, attestation, grant, resource, or audit event, and revocation creation, the existing revocation reads, the coverage summary, and the existing error JSON are unchanged. `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, and `POST` on this route are rejected with `405 method_not_allowed`.
159	
160	## Auditable revocation-impact checkpoint export and stateless verification
161	
162	Reviewers can export the full filtered revocation-impact snapshot as a self-contained package with an integrity checkpoint, and a third party can verify a received package offline from its body alone. Both routes are strictly read-only/pure: neither writes any resource, audit row, or log.
163	
164	- `GET /v1/revocation-impact-package?attestation_id=...&revoker_actor_id=...&reason=...&from=...&to=...` — read-only one-call export of the filtered revocation-impact snapshot together with its auditable checkpoint. It accepts exactly the five revocation-impact search filters with the exact-match, strict RFC 3339 UTC, repeated-parameter, and undeclared-parameter semantics of the `GET /v1/revocation-impacts` route; `limit` and `cursor` are not accepted (the package always covers the entire filtered set with no pagination), and blank/illegal/repeated/undeclared parameters and a `from` later than `to` are all `422 validation_error`, validated before any revocation is read. The request carries no body: any body bytes (even whitespace, arbitrary bytes, or malformed JSON) are `422 validation_error`, rejected before any query parameter or revocation record is read. The success body is compact UTF-8 JSON (compact separators, unescaped non-ASCII) terminated by exactly one newline, strictly `{"checkpoint", "impacts"}` in that member order: `checkpoint` is exactly `{"checkpoint_version", "digest_algorithm", "impact_count", "impacts_digest_hex"}` with `checkpoint_version="provenance-revocation-impact-checkpoint-v1"`, `digest_algorithm="sha256"`, the total number of matched impacts, and the digest below; `impacts` lists, in the revocations' stable creation order (`created_at` with the persistent insertion-order tiebreaker), the existing revocation-impact public views matched by that same filter — each item exactly the 13 fields served by `GET /v1/revocation-impacts` (the revocation public view plus `content_id`, `target_type`, `signer_actor_id`, the after/before qualified-signer counts and coverage statuses, and `qualified_signer_count_delta`); no raw signature, signature digest, public key, claim payload, content byte, or evidence byte is ever included. `impacts_digest_hex` is the SHA-256 hex digest over exactly the `impacts` array returned in the same response: the array keeps its element order, every nested object's keys are sorted by Unicode code point, and serialization uses compact separators, unescaped non-ASCII, and UTF-8 encoding, so the digest is reproducible by an external verifier from the package body alone; both halves derive from a single read-only state read, so they are always mutually consistent and the returned pair verifies via the stateless verification route below. An empty match set is still a legal snapshot: `"impacts": []`, `impact_count: 0`, and the deterministic digest of the empty array. Filter values are never resolved for existence, so an unknown or nonexistent value yields that empty snapshot rather than a 404. Repeated reads and reads across an app restart return the same package for the same persisted state. The route is strictly read-only — success, empty results, and failures create, modify, or delete no revocation, attestation, grant, resource, or audit event — and revocation creation, the existing revocation reads, the impact search, and the existing error JSON are unchanged. `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, and `POST` on this route are rejected with `405 method_not_allowed`.
165	- `POST /v1/impact-verifications` — stateless offline verification of a received revocation-impact package, for third-party verifiers. The request body is exactly `{"checkpoint", "impacts"}` with the field structure of the export's public view: `checkpoint` is exactly `{"checkpoint_version", "digest_algorithm", "impact_count", "impacts_digest_hex"}` with `checkpoint_version="provenance-revocation-impact-checkpoint-v1"`, `digest_algorithm="sha256"`, a non-negative integer `impact_count`, and an `impacts_digest_hex` of exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters; `impacts` is an array of exactly `impact_count` items, each carrying exactly the exported 13 impact fields with strict types — non-empty case/whitespace-sensitive strings for the identifiers and `reason`, a strict RFC 3339 UTC `created_at` (`Z` or `+00:00`, seconds required, no naive or non-UTC value), `target_type` exactly `claim` or `evidence_bundle`, each coverage status exactly `uncovered`, `partial`, or `covered`, and non-negative integral counts — and internally consistent before/after coverage fields: `qualified_signer_count_after` never exceeds `qualified_signer_count_before`, `qualified_signer_count_delta` equals exactly `before - after` and is `0` or `1`, and each coverage status matches its signer count under the evidence-coverage rules (a positive count is always `covered`; a zero count is `uncovered` or `partial`). No undeclared member is accepted on any object, so no raw signature, public key, payload, content, or evidence field can enter the request. The digest is recomputed over `impacts` exactly as received (array order preserved, nested object keys sorted by Unicode code point, compact separators, unescaped non-ASCII, UTF-8, SHA-256). A match returns `200` with exactly `{"valid": true}` and no other field; a structurally valid request whose recomputed digest differs returns `200` with exactly `{"valid": false, "computed_digest_hex": ...}`. Malformed JSON; a missing, extra, null, or wrong-typed top-level or nested field; the wrong version/algorithm; a malformed digest or timestamp; an array whose length differs from `impact_count`; and an internally inconsistent impact (a violated delta/count/status association) are all `422 validation_error`. The route accepts no query parameters — any parameter is `422 validation_error`. It is purely a function of the request body: it never queries, creates, or modifies any local revocation record or other resource, writes no audit row or log, and never resolves any identifier, so unknown resources, repeated identical requests, and differing local state all produce the same verdict; fabricated but structurally consistent identifiers verify exactly like known ones. The success body is compact UTF-8 JSON (compact separators, unescaped non-ASCII) terminated by exactly one newline; times stay UTC and every count renders as an integer. The existing revocation creation, revocation retrieval and single-record read, the impact search, and the existing error JSON semantics are unchanged.
166	
167	## Controlled revocation-impact import, receipt read, receipt search, and current-state reconciliation
168	
169	A reviewer who received a revocation-impact package and verified it offline can register that checkpoint with the service, read back the immutable receipt, search every registered receipt, and reconcile a receipt against the current local impact set. Registration is a pure function of the request body: the described impacts are never created, modified, or queried against local state, and no raw material is persisted.
170	
171	- `POST /v1/impact-imports` — controlled registration of an offline-verified revocation-impact checkpoint. The request body is exactly `{"checkpoint", "impacts"}`, with the field structure, fixed version/algorithm, impact count, strict RFC 3339 UTC timestamps, internal before/after coverage associations, and canonical digest rules of the stateless `POST /v1/impact-verifications` route: `checkpoint` is exactly `{"checkpoint_version", "digest_algorithm", "impact_count", "impacts_digest_hex"}` with `checkpoint_version="provenance-revocation-impact-checkpoint-v1"`, `digest_algorithm="sha256"`, a non-negative integer `impact_count`, and a 64-lowercase-hex `impacts_digest_hex`; `impacts` is an array of exactly `impact_count` items, each exactly the exported 13-field impact public view. 197	## Read-only proof access grants
198	
199	A read-only access grant authorizes another actor to read one existing attestation through a protected endpoint. Grants are immutable and append-only: there is no update or delete path, and a grant never mutates the attestation it references.
200	
201	Both protected routes authenticate every request with three headers:
202	
203	- `X-PA` — the calling actor id;
204	- `X-PT` — the request timestamp as an RFC 3339 UTC instant (`Z` or an explicit `+00:00`; no naive or non-UTC value), no more than **300 seconds** from the server's current time;
205	- `X-PS` — a standard-Base64 Ed25519 signature (64 raw bytes) over the exact UTF-8 compact JSON array (compact separators, non-ASCII emitted unescaped):
206	
207	  ```
208	  ["provenance-access-v1",method,path,timestamp,body_sha256]
209	  ```
210	
211	  `method` is the uppercase HTTP method, `path` is the request path without any query string, `timestamp` is the exact `X-PT` header value, and `body_sha256` is the lowercase-hex SHA-256 of the actual request body bytes — the digest of zero bytes for an empty (GET) body. The signature is accepted if it verifies under **any** public key of a non-revoked attestation created by the calling actor; a revoked attestation's key never authenticates.
212	
213	- `POST /v1/attestation-access-grants` — JSON body contains exactly `attestation_id` and `grantee_actor_id`; any undeclared field is rejected. Only the attestation's `signer_actor_id` (authenticated as above) may create a grant. The first creation returns `201` with exactly `{id, attestation_id, grantee_actor_id, created_at}` — a stable `aag_` id and a UTC `created_at`. A retried submission for the same `(attestation_id, grantee_actor_id)` pair returns `200` with the original record and writes no new row or audit event; a different grantee forms an independent, immutable record. The first grant write and its `attestation.access_granted` audit event commit in a single transaction. Missing credentials, an unparseable or out-of-window timestamp, malformed signature encoding, a signature no current key of the actor verifies, malformed fields or JSON, a missing attestation, a missing grantee actor, and a caller who is not the attestation's signer are all `422 validation_error`; no failure writes a resource or an audit event.
214	- `GET /v1/protected/attestations/{attestation_id}` — read-only. Only the attestation's `signer_actor_id` or an actor holding an access grant for that exact attestation may call it; success returns the existing attestation's public view (the same fields as `GET /v1/attestations/{id}`). A missing target, an unauthenticated caller, and an unauthorized caller all return the **same opaque `404 not_found`**, so existence is never revealed to a caller without access. An unparseable/out-of-window timestamp or a signature that is not canonical Base64 of exactly 64 bytes is `422 validation_error`. The read writes no resource and no audit event.
215	- `GET /v1/attestations/{attestation_id}/access-grants` — read-only, signed with the same `X-PA`/`X-PT`/`X-PS` contract over the empty GET body (the signed path carries no query string). Only the attestation's `signer_actor_id` may call it — a grantee who can read the protected proof cannot list its grants. A missing or unauthenticatable credential, a missing target, and a non-signer all return the **same opaque `404 not_found`**; an unparseable/out-of-window timestamp or a malformed signature is `422 validation_error`. Success is strictly `{"items", "count", "next_cursor"}`; each item carries exactly `{id, attestation_id, grantee_actor_id, created_at}` in stable creation order (`created_at` with the monotonic sequence tiebreaker) and never echoes any revocation, private key, raw signature, authentication header, payload, or byte. Only `limit` and `cursor` are accepted: `limit` is a pure decimal integer in `1..100` (default `50`); any undeclared, repeated, blank/whitespace, or otherwise illegal parameter — and any malformed, unsigned, foreign-family, or non-binding cursor — is `422 validation_error`, checked before the target lookup. The opaque cursor is HMAC-signed and bound to the attestation, the authenticated caller, and the effective limit, so it resumes only the query that minted it; continuation pages repeat and omit nothing, the last page carries `next_cursor: null`, and a position past the tail returns `"items": []` with the same `count`. An attestation without grants returns an empty collection; the route is strictly read-only and leaves the existing grant and protected-read interfaces unchanged.
216	
217	### Read-only tracking of grant revocations
218	
219	Reviewers can read the immutable grant-revocation records through three read-only routes. None requires the `X-PA`/`X-PT`/`X-PS` headers. The single-record and per-grant routes accept **no query parameters** — any, blank, or repeated parameter is `422 validation_error` validated *before* the resource lookup. All three are strictly read-only: a successful read, an empty result, a missing resource, and a parameter failure create or modify no grant, revocation, other resource, or audit event.
220	
221	- `GET /v1/attestation-access-grant-revocations/{revocation_id}` — returns one existing revocation's public view, exactly `{id, grant_id, revoker_actor_id, reason, created_at}` with a UTC timestamp. The revocation id is the only lookup key — a grant id or attestation id is never reverse-resolved. An unknown id is an explicit `404 attestation_access_grant_revocation_not_found` carrying the requested `revocation_id` (an unknown id supplied together with a query parameter is the 422, since parameters are checked first). The view carries no private key, raw signature, authentication header, claim payload, content, or evidence byte.
222	- `GET /v1/attestation-access-grants/{grant_id}/revocations` — returns only that existing grant's revocation records as strictly `{"items", "count"}`, each item the exact five-field public view above, in the records' stable creation order (`created_at` with the monotonic sequence tiebreaker). The grant id is the sole lookup key — records are never resolved through a revoker, reason, attestation, or revocation id. An unknown grant is `422 validation_error` with `details.reason="grant_not_found"` (the same boundary as the revocation write route), never an empty collection and never a reverse lookup; an existing grant that has not been revoked returns `{"items": [], "count": 0}`. Repeated reads are deterministic and the views are unchanged across an app restart.
223	- `GET /v1/attestation-access-grant-revocations?grant_id=...&revoker_actor_id=...&reason=...&from=...&to=...&limit=...&cursor=...` — global read-only cross-grant search over the immutable grant-revocation records. Only `GET` is served (`POST` remains the authenticated creation route; `PUT`/`PATCH`/`DELETE` are `405 method_not_allowed`). The request body must be empty: carrying any bytes (whitespace, arbitrary bytes, or malformed JSON included) is `422 validation_error`, validated before any query parameter or revocation record is read. The success body is compact UTF-8 JSON (compact separators, unescaped non-ASCII) terminated by exactly one newline, with members in exactly the order `items`, `count`, `next_cursor`; each item reuses the single-revocation public view above in the records' stable creation order (`created_at`, with the persistence insertion order breaking same-instant ties, stable across restarts) and never returns a raw signature, private key, payload, content, or evidence byte. Optional `grant_id`, `revoker_actor_id`, and `reason` are non-empty, case- and whitespace-sensitive value comparisons; each filter is accepted at most once and all combine as logical AND (absent means unfiltered). Unknown or nonexistent filter values only produce an empty collection, never a 404, and an undeclared filter name is a 422 (never a 404). `from` and `to` accept only strict RFC 3339 UTC creation instants (`Z` or `+00:00`, inclusive bounds), and `from` must not be later than `to`. `count` is the filtered total covering every page, independent of the page returned. `limit` is a pure decimal integer from 1 to 100 defaulting to 50 — an empty, signed, fractional, exponent, or whitespace-bearing value is rejected, never defaulted. `cursor` is an opaque HMAC-signed server token in its own `gr1` family, signed by the server and bound to every effective filter (including `null` filters) and the effective limit, so a continuation only resumes the exact query that minted it: the first page carries no `cursor`, a continuation carries the previous `next_cursor` with the same conditions, and consecutive pages never repeat or omit an item. Replaying a cursor returns the same continuation page; the final page carries `next_cursor: null`, and a cursor at or past the tail returns empty `items` with the original `count`. A blank, whitespace-only, malformed, tampered, cross-entry/foreign-family, wrong-claim-set, or filter/limit-misbound cursor is `422 validation_error`, as is an empty, illegal, repeated, or undeclared parameter. All validation completes before any revocation record is read. No match returns `{"items": [], "count": 0, "next_cursor": null}`. Numbers are rendered as integers only (no negative zero or non-finite values). Success, empty results, and failures are strictly read-only: no record or audit event is created or modified, and revocation creation, the single-record read, the per-grant listing, and the existing error JSON are unchanged.
224	
225	## Content lineage relations
226	
227	Relations record how content identities descend from one another: `content_id` is the newer version or derived content, `parent_content_id` is its direct source, and `relation_type` is `version_of` or `derived_from`. Relations are immutable and append-only: there is no update or delete path.
228	
229	- `POST /v1/content-relations` — create a relation between two existing contents. The first creation returns `201` with the stable `rel_` id, both content ids, the relation type, and a UTC `created_at`; a repeat submission of the same three fields returns `200` with the existing relation and writes no row or audit event. An unknown content on either side is `404 content_not_found`; blank identifiers, an unknown relation type, a self-loop, or an edge that would close a lineage cycle are `422 validation_error` and write nothing.
230	- `GET /v1/content-relations/{relation_id}` — full public fields, or `404 content_relation_not_found`.
231	- `GET /v1/content-relations?id=...&content_id=...&parent_content_id=...&relation_type=...&from=...&to=...&limit=...&cursor=...` — global read-only search across the immutable lineage relations. Returns `{"items", "count", "next_cursor"}` where each item reuses the single-relation public view (`id`, `content_id`, `parent_content_id`, `relation_type`, UTC `created_at`). Records are returned in stable creation order (`created_at`, with the persistence insertion order breaking same-instant ties, stable across restarts). Optional `id`, `content_id`, and `parent_content_id` are non-empty, case/whitespace-sensitive exact matches; optional `relation_type` accepts only the literals `version_of` and `derived_from`. Every filter combines as logical AND — an unknown or nonexistent value yields an empty collection, never a 404; `from` and `to` are strict RFC 3339 UTC instants applied as inclusive `created_at` bounds, and `from` must not be later than `to`. `limit` is a pure decimal integer from 1 to 100 defaulting to 50; `cursor` is an opaque HMAC-signed server token (its own `rl1` family) binding to every effective filter and the limit, so pages resume without duplication or omission, `count` is always the filtered total across all pages, the first page carries no cursor, and the final and past-the-tail pages carry `next_cursor: null` with an empty page at or past the tail. Blank, wrong-typed, malformed, out-of-range, repeated, or undeclared parameters; an invalid `relation_type`; a `from` later than `to`; an empty, malformed, tampered, foreign-family, or filter/limit-mismatching `cursor`; and any non-empty request body (whitespace, arbitrary bytes, or bad JSON included) are all `422 validation_error`, validated before any relation record is read and never returning partial results. No matching records yields an empty collection. The request body must be empty. Success, empty results, and failures are strictly read-only: no relation or audit event is created, modified, or deleted; relation creation idempotency, self-loop/cycle rejection, the detail and per-content reads, lineage traversal, and the existing error JSON are unchanged. `PUT`, `PATCH`, and `DELETE` on this route are rejected with `405 method_not_allowed`.
